skill.name: c-pro
skill.description: Develop reliable C99 and C11 systems code with explicit memory ownership, defensive error handling, debugging, testing, and performance practices.
skill.summary: Build efficient, maintainable C systems software with disciplined memory management and validation.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: C systems work can fail through leaks, unchecked calls, and poor portability. This skill guides robust C99/C11 implementation, testing, debugging, and performance validation.
actual_capabilities: Designs C99 and C11 code with explicit memory ownership and balanced allocation cleanup.
Adds defensive return-value checks and error handling for allocations and system calls.
Structures headers, include guards, Makefiles, and compiler warning flags.
Guides POSIX, pthread, embedded, pointer, and data-structure implementation decisions.
Proposes CUnit tests, Valgrind checks, debugger workflows, and relevant benchmarks.
Reviews stack usage, resource constraints, and measured performance before optimization.
limitations: Generated code still requires compilation and testing on the target compiler, operating system, and hardware.
The skill does not execute Valgrind, GDB, clang-tidy, tests, or benchmarks by itself.
Platform-specific APIs outside C99, C11, and common POSIX patterns may require additional expertise.
It cannot prove memory safety, thread safety, real-time behavior, or performance from source text alone.

use_cases.title: Learn Safe Memory Ownership
use_cases.description: Explain allocation, ownership, cleanup paths, and pointer use for a small C program.

use_cases.title: Harden POSIX Components
use_cases.description: Review system calls, pthread synchronization, error handling, headers, and tests for production services.

use_cases.title: Optimize Constrained Firmware
use_cases.description: Reduce stack and heap pressure, identify measurable bottlenecks, and preserve portability on constrained targets.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Memory Ownership
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain memory ownership for [task]. Identify allocations, owners, lifetimes, cleanup paths, and failure cases using C99 conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner guidance for a small C feature

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Defensive Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [component] in C11 for [platform]. Include headers, ownership rules, checked return values, cleanup logic, compiler flags, and focused tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrent POSIX Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided pthread code for races, deadlocks, resource leaks, and unchecked calls. Propose corrections and a reproducible validation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Profile an Embedded System
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [embedded workload] under [memory and timing limits]. Prioritize measured bottlenecks, bounded resource use, portability, benchmarks, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: Review a linked-list insertion function that allocates nodes and can fail.
output: Ownership map identifying the caller, list, and temporary allocation responsibilities.
Failure-path review covering allocation errors, unchanged list state, and cleanup.
Test plan for empty lists, allocation failure, repeated insertion, and complete destruction.

output_examples.input: Plan a bounded producer-consumer queue for a POSIX service.
output: Synchronization design using one mutex, condition variables, and explicit shutdown state.
Error-handling checklist for initialization, waits, thread creation, and partial cleanup.
Validation plan covering race detection, saturation, shutdown, and repeated startup.

output_examples.input: Reduce memory use in firmware without changing observable behavior.
output_examples.output: A measurement-first plan compares stack, heap, and static storage, then prioritizes verified reductions with regression and timing checks.

best_practices: State ownership and lifetime rules before implementing allocations or shared data structures.
Compile with strict warnings and validate using tests, static analysis, debugging tools, and leak checks.
Profile representative workloads before optimizing, then preserve behavior with regression benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Do not return unverified code without checking allocation failures, system-call results, and cleanup paths.
Do not optimize from assumptions when target measurements and resource limits are unavailable.
Do not claim portability, memory safety, or thread safety without environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Which C standards does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets C99 and C11, with POSIX guidance when the task requires operating-system interfaces.

faq.question: Can it help with memory leaks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can trace ownership and cleanup paths, but Valgrind or equivalent target testing must confirm the result.

faq.question: Does it support embedded development?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers stack limits, heap pressure, deterministic resource use, portability, and hardware constraints.

faq.question: Can it review multithreaded C?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess pthread synchronization, races, deadlocks, shutdown behavior, and resource cleanup.

faq.question: Will it generate build and test guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Outputs may include Makefile flags, header organization, CUnit tests, debugging steps, and benchmark plans.

faq.question: Does it execute compilers or analysis tools?
faq.answer: No. Tool execution depends on the connected agent environment and user permissions.
